Manu Govind, Sc, The Kerala Veterinary And Animal Sciences University This Writ Appeal Having Come Up For Admission On 04.08.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: W.A.No.1273 of 2025 3 2025:Ker:58015 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner has also sought for a writ of mandamus commanding the 1st respondent University to recognise her B.Com degree of the Mini.T.K vs The Kerala Veterinary And Animal ... on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158029373/ 2 University of Calicut as sufficient to meet the educational qualification for applying to the Diploma course in Livestock Management. The document marked as Ext.P2 is a copy of the degree certificate issued by the University of Calicut, which is one dated 05.12.2015. In the writ petition it is stated that the petitioner successfully completed B.Com degree course conducted by the University of Calicut, under the Distance Education Scheme. The document marked as Ext.P1 is a notification dated 02.10.2024 issued by the 1st respondent University inviting applications for Diploma course in Livestock Management, which is a course intended for Class III and Class IV permanent employees of the University. The qualifications prescribed in the said notification for admission to Diploma course in Livestock Management are as follows; "1) Plus Two 2) A minimum of three years regular service in the University" Mini.T.K vs The Kerala Veterinary And Animal ... on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158029373/ 3 9. Along with this writ appeal, the appellant-petitioner has placed on record Annexure A1 certificate dated 25.03.2025 issued by the Assistant Registrar of the University of Calicut, in which it is certified as follows; "Certified that Mrs. Mini.T.K was a student of the Centre for Distance and Online Education (Formerly known as School of Distance Education), University of Calicut for B.Com course (Open stream) during A.Y, 2000-2003 with Enrolment No: 002385 & Reg No: 22325. She was admitted to first year B. Com course in 2000 on the basis 2025:KER:58015 of an entrance test conducted by this University. Requisite qualification for appearing to the Entrance Examination was completion 18 years of age by the applicant as on July 1st of that particular year. The Entrance Examination was conducted by the University as per the rules and regulations of the UGC Act 1956 vide notification No. F1-8/92 (CPP-II) dated 04.11.1995. The Sylabus, Scheme, Exam, Mark list etc. for Open and Regular course are one and the same. The Hon. High court of Kerala vide OP No. 590 of 1995T has ordered that Open BA/B.Com degree is equivalent to the Regular BA/B.Com degree in all respects.
texts.arguments: 10. Before the learned Single Judge relying on the decision of the Apex Court in Jyothi K.K. v. Kerala Public Service Commission [(2010) 15 SCC 596] the appellant- petitioner contended that B.Com degree being a higher qualification than the educational qualification of Plus Two prescribed in Ext.P1 notification for admission to Diploma course in Livestock Management, she is eligible for admission to the said course, since a higher qualification must presuppose acquisition of a lower qualification. 11. In Jyothi K.K. [(2010) 15 SCC 596], the Apex Court, in the context of eligibility criteria in the recruitment process held that, normally qualification prescribed in the relevant rules should not be whittled down and different 2025:KER:58015 qualification cannot be adopted. There was however a statutory provision, i.e., Rule 10(a)(ii) of the Kerala State and Subordinate Service Rules, 1956 which provided that such of those higher qualifications which presuppose acquisition of the lower qualification prescribed for the post shall also be sufficient for the post. Thus, if a candidate has acquired higher qualification in the same faculty or discipline, such qualification presupposes acquisition of (lower) qualification prescribed for the post. 12. In Chandra Shekhar Singh v. State of Jharkhand [2025 SCC OnLine SC 595], another decision relied on by the learned counsel for the appellant, the Apex Court, in the context of recruitment to the post of Food Safety Officers in the State of Jharkhand reiterated that a candidate possessing a higher degree of qualification cannot be rejected solely because a lower degree or qualification is required for a particular post. The eligibility criteria, i.e., the educational qualification of Plus Two prescribed in the said notification is for admission to Diploma course in Livestock Management, conducted by the 1st respondent University for employees having minimum three 2025:KER:58015 years' service in the University, for being considered for appointment by transfer to the post of Farm Assistant Gr.II. An employee of the 1st respondent University, in order to get admission to Diploma course in Livestock Management should possess the educational qualification of Plus Two prescribed in Ext.P1 notification. The appellant-petitioner, who possess B.Com degree from the University of Calicut under Distance Education Scheme, without 10+2+3 pattern, cannot be said to be a candidate possessing the required educational qualification of Plus Two prescribed in the said notification for admission to Diploma course in Livestock Management.
